articles.title: Mom ‘very invested’ in Lindsay Clancy case hires Casey Anthony attorney after allegedly killing son: docs
articles.summary: Corie Walsh allegedly texted friends about the Lindsay Clancy murder trial just hours before her 2-year-old son Barrett was found dead in Frankfort.
articles.body: A Frankfort, Illinois, mother accused of killing her 2-year-old son had been discussing the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial with friends just hours before the boy was found dead, court documents allege, and has hired one of Casey Anthony's former attorneys to defend her. Corie A. Walsh, 38, later told officers she killed her son because she believed he was the "devil" and the "anti-Christ," a petition seeking to deny her pretrial release obtained by Fox 32 in Chicago states. Walsh has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the death of her son, Barrett Walsh. The filing mentions her interest in the Clancy case but does not allege that it was connected to Barrett’s death. ILLINOIS MOTHER CHARGED WITH MURDER IN DEATH OF 2-YEAR-OLD SON IN CASE DRAWING COMPARISONS TO LINDSAY CLANCY Walsh’s attorney, Andrea Lyon, said she was "psychotic" and rejected any connection between her client’s interest in the Clancy case and the alleged killing. "They are not correlated at all. It’s just accidental," Lyon said, calling speculation that Walsh’s actions were a copycat crime "baseless and cruel." Court documents show Frankfort police officers were called to a home in the 22700 block of Brook Stone Court just after 4 p.m. Sept. 1 for a report of an injured child. Upon arrival, officers found a neighbor performing CPR on Barrett after she reportedly discovered the toddler hanging from a basement rafter with his feet off the ground. SUBURBAN ILLINOIS BOY DIES IN SUSPECTED DOMESTIC HOMICIDE AS NEIGHBORS FEAR ANOTHER LINDSAY CLANCY CASE The neighbor brought Barrett down, laid him on the floor and attempted CPR while calling 911, later telling police the boy was cold and had no pulse. Barrett was pronounced dead at the scene, and a preliminary autopsy determined he died of asphyxia caused by strangulation, according to the filing. Walsh’s three other children were unharmed, including an infant who was in the house at the time and two school-aged children who returned home around the time Barrett was found. Her husband was traveling out of state when the incident occurred and flew home that evening. While officers were at the house, they were directed to an upstairs master bathroom where Walsh was reportedly trying to harm herself. LINDSAY CLANCY MISTRIAL DECLARED AFTER JURY DEADLOCKS IN KILLINGS OF HER THREE CHILDREN The petition states Walsh was lying fully dressed in a bathtub surrounded by bloody water while a neighbor held a towel against her left inner thigh. The neighbor told investigators she had disarmed Walsh of a knife and thrown it into a sink. Police recovered the knife into evidence while documenting cuts on Walsh’s wrists and thighs, court documents state. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The neighbor told investigators that Walsh asked why she had taken the knife from her because she was trying to kill herself. Walsh then said "Bear" was in the basement – referencing a known nickname for Barrett, the petition notes. LINDSAY CLANCY DESCRIBED A MALE VOICE ORDERING HER TO ‘KILL HER CHILDREN AND KILL HERSELF’: TESTIMONY While hospitalized, Walsh made additional statements to investigators describing how she killed the toddler, which prosecutors noted were consistent with the physical evidence. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Witnesses told investigators Walsh had recently become "very invested" in the Clancy murder trial, which involved a Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE Walsh allegedly discussed the Clancy case in a group text message with friends as recently as 12:30 p.m. Sept. 1 – roughly three and a half hours before Barrett was found. Her cellphone was recovered from the bathroom, and forensic analysis of the device was ongoing as of Sept. 3. SEND US A TIP Prosecutors are asking a judge to deny Walsh pretrial release, arguing that she poses a real and present threat to her husband and her three surviving children. Walsh faces three counts of first-degree murder, with prosecutors outlining different legal theories regarding her intent. Because Barrett was 2 years old, a conviction carries a mandatory sentence of 60 to 100 years in prison without the possibility of early release. Walsh remains hospitalized at Silver Cross Hospital and is expected to be transferred to the Will County Adult Detention Facility once medically released. ACCUSED NC KILLER MOM PLANS INSANITY DEFENSE — AS RETIRED JUDGE SAYS MORE MAY FOLLOW LINDSAY CLANCY STRATEGY Walsh’s defense team includes attorney Lyon, who previously represented Anthony. In 2011, Anthony was acquitted in the death of her 2-year-old daughter, Caylee, whose death remains unsolved. A jury found Anthony guilty of lying to law enforcement but not guilty of first-degree murder, aggravated manslaughter or aggravated child abuse. The Will County State’s Attorney’s Office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. At a detention hearing Tuesday, a judge denied Walsh’s request for pretrial release to a locked hospital setting. Lyon said the defense was disappointed but would continue investigating the case while Walsh recovers from her wounds. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Lyon said the defense will argue that Walsh was psychotic and that the charges do not amount to first-degree murder. "She was psychotic. And this is not a first-degree murder," she told reporters. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL The defense may seek pretrial release again, Lyon said. articles.title: Trapped Baby Elephant Cries Out Until Rescuers Arrive With a Lifeline
articles.summary: A baby elephant trapped alone in a muddy well in Tanzania cried out as it struggled to escape, and the clock was ticking before predators or exhaustion could...
articles.body:
A baby elephant became trapped in a muddy livestock watering well in northern Tanzania and had to be rescued by a team before reuniting with its family.

The rescue team used a vehicle equipped with a winch to carefully pull the young elephant out of the pit, ensuring its safety and preventing further distress.

Newborn elephant calves can weigh hundreds of pounds at birth, with adult African savanna elephants growing to be the largest living land animals, making rescues of trapped elephants a challenging and specialized operation.

Life in the wild comes with a long list of daily challenges. Animals need reliable access to food and water, safe places to rest, and ways to avoid threats. For a young animal that becomes trapped, those ordinary challenges can suddenly become much more serious.

That is exactly what happened to the baby elephant in the video above. The calf became stuck in a muddy livestock watering well in northern Tanzania and could not climb back out on its own. Fortunately, people nearby spotted the animal and called in a rescue team before the situation got worse.

The footage shared by We Love Animals takes us to the Enduimet Wildlife Management Area in northern Tanzania, part of the Greater Amboseli ecosystem in Africa . Big Life Foundation reported that the calf had fallen into a man-made livestock watering well while trying to drink. We Love Animals shares rescue and wildlife footage involving everything from elephants to foxes , dogs , and even a swan .

As the video begins, we see the young elephant trapped below ground and vocalizing repeatedly as it struggles to escape. Elephant calves are normally protected by their family groups , and becoming separated can leave a young elephant much more vulnerable.

Large wildlife rescues are also dangerous for the animal and the people trying to help. General animal-rescue guidance from the West Midlands Fire Service emphasizes getting appropriate rescue professionals involved when an animal is trapped or injured. In the wild, young elephants can also be vulnerable to predators such as lions and hyenas, particularly when separated from the protection of their herd.

Fortunately for this calf, help was not far away. Representatives from Royal African Safaris discovered the trapped elephant and alerted a Big Life-funded rapid-response ranger unit. The rescuers brought in a vehicle equipped with a winch and worked together to get a cable around the calf.

Once everything was in place, the team carefully used the vehicle winch to pull the elephant out of the muddy pit. The story got even better from there. According to Big Life Foundation, the calf picked up the scent of its family and headed after them. The herd had moved only a few kilometers away, allowing the young elephant to reunite with its mother and family.

Even though the elephant in the video is a calf, that does not mean it is small. According to SeaWorld , newborn elephant calves average about 3 feet tall and 264 pounds at birth. Newborn male African elephants can weigh as much as 364 pounds.

And they only get bigger from there. African savanna elephants are the largest living land animals. Adult males can stand around 13 feet tall at the shoulder and weigh more than 13,000 pounds. Pulling a calf weighing a few hundred pounds from a muddy well is already a serious undertaking. Trying the same thing with a full-grown elephant would be an entirely different rescue operation.

articles.title: Just 1% of asylum seekers in UK genuine, insider says, as UN blasts Britain for allowing bogus claims
articles.summary: UK News: TOI correspondent from London: “At best 1% of asylum seekers in the UK are genuine,” a home office whistleblower has said, adding that most claims are.
articles.body: TOI correspondent from London: “At best 1% of asylum seekers in the UK are genuine,” a home office whistleblower has said, adding that most claims are scripted and bogus but still get granted.The United Nations refugee agency has criticised the home office, too, over risks that migrants are being granted asylum in the UK “even though they are not entitled to it” after finding in an audit that in a third of cases the “full basis of the applicant’s claim remained unclear”.The home office official, who worked for years as a decision-maker on asylum claims, told the UK Times newspaper: “There’s almost no aspect of the asylum system that isn’t either a massive fraud or just really dysfunctional.”He said many asylum seekers used the “same script” but staff won’t check their claims with their country of origin, as doing so could place individuals at risk.He saw hundreds of claims from Pakistani asylum seekers saying they are gay who all claimed to have the same boyfriend – a man who has provided hundreds of “very obviously fake letters of support” to all of them.The men all submitted photographs from the same London gay venue, Legs 800 Club, which closed permanently last year, standing topless with their arms around each other.A large number of Bangladeshi asylum seekers in recent years have been claiming they faced political persecution in Bangladesh because of their membership of the Awami League, the whistleblower said.Yet despite claiming to hold senior positions in the Awami League, or its student wing, Chhatra, they were unable to provide any substantive details about its policies and could only cite its slogan.A large number of Iraqi Kurds claiming asylum said they had been in a relationship with the same daughter of the prime minister of the Kurdistan region, he said, adding that this had become a “running joke” among colleagues.In the year ending June 2026, Indians were the eighth top nationality to claim asylum in Britain, making 4,964 claims.UK-born PIO Gujarati-origin former British diplomat Ameer Kotecha said: “How on earth can there be almost 5,000 asylum seekers from India? India is treated by the home office as a designated safe state.”“Almost all of these claims from Indian nationals will be bogus,” Kotecha claimed.A home office spokesperson said they “do not comment on anonymous briefings”.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 70 Americans still unaccounted for after catastrophic Nepal flooding
articles.summary: Officials say 70 Americans remain unaccounted for after catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border, while warning the region remains too dangerous for travelers.
articles.body: The State Department said Tuesday it is aware of approximately 70 Americans who remain unaccounted for in the Nepal-China border region following last month's catastrophic flooding, while 18 Americans have now made it to safety. "We extend our deepest sympathy to all those affected by the flooding in Nepal, and their families, and we reaffirm our enduring friendship with the Nepali people," a State Department official told Fox News. "The Department of State remains in close contact with the families of Americans who remain unaccounted for and is committed to providing regular updates as more information becomes available." ROUGHLY 80 AMERICANS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR AFTER HIMALAYAN DISASTER KILLS 903, OFFICIALS SAY Officials also urged Americans not to travel to the disaster zone, warning the region remains at risk for additional flash floods and landslides. The latest update reduced the number of Americans unaccounted for from 75 to 70, while the number confirmed safe rose from 16 to 18. Officials have not confirmed any American deaths. RESCUERS USE ZIPLINES TO TRANSPORT TRAPPED CITIZENS AFTER DEVASTATING NEPAL FLOODS DECIMATE COUNTRY'S BRIDGES As search efforts continue, Nepalese authorities said rescuers are concentrating on three hydropower project tunnels where they believe dozens of workers may still be trapped beneath debris left by the Aug. 26 glacier collapse that triggered devastating flooding along the Nepal-China border, according to Reuters. "Our search operation is focused on finding survivors, including in tunnels. Our bigger focus is on the Chilime hydroelectric project, where we believe people are trapped, because there was a canteen, residency and arrangements for food," Dharma Raj Upreti, chief of Nepal's disaster authority, told Reuters. DEATH TOLL FROM MUDSLIDES, FLOODING AT NEPAL-CHINA BORDER CLIMBS PAST 670; NEARLY 3,000 MISSING CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The disaster has killed at least 1,399 people across Nepal and China's Tibet region, with more than 5,400 others still missing, according to authorities. Both governments have blamed climate change for the glacier collapse that unleashed the flooding. Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nicolas Cage’s $10.5 million Malibu mansion hit by massive sinkhole as driveway collapses amid coastal erosion; photos show 30ft-wide crater outside his 4,000-square-foot beachfront home
articles.summary: US News: Hollywood star Nicolas Cage’s $10.5 million Malibu mansion has been hit by a dramatic sinkhole after part of the property’s driveway collapsed, with t.
articles.body: Hollywood star Nicolas Cage’s $10.5 million Malibu mansion has been hit by a dramatic sinkhole after part of the property’s driveway collapsed, with the damage coming amid heavy rain, high surf and suspected coastal erosion along Southern California’s coastline.Photos from the scene show a huge crater where the driveway of the 4,000-square-foot beachfront property once stood. Sections of asphalt and concrete appear to have cracked and fallen into the hole, while debris, parts of a privacy fence and a portable toilet were also swallowed by the collapse. Large chunks of concrete could be seen inside the crater.Sinkhole is around 30 feet by 30 feetAccording to KTLA, firefighters came upon the chaotic scene early Tuesday while responding to a report of a suspected gas main break. A public information officer told the outlet that the massive hole, believed to have been caused by coastal erosion, measures around 30 feet by 30 feet.Gas company workers were also at the property working to restore the damaged gas main.Despite the scale of the collapse, the outlet reported that no evacuations had been ordered and no injuries were reported. The local outlet also noted that no one appeared to be home when the driveway gave way.KTLA reporter Rich Prickett said while reporting from the scene that the house appeared to be undergoing some sort of renovation.Workers wearing orange safety vests could be seen assessing the damage, while a firetruck was photographed near the residence with a yellow hose extended from the vehicle.Nicolas Cage bought the Malibu mansion for $10.5 million in 2024Cage purchased the beachfront property in 2024 for $10.5 million. According to Realtor, the contemporary home spans approximately 4,000 square feet and boasts dramatic ocean views and a private rooftop deck.The four-level residence features floor-to-ceiling glass, multiple ocean-facing terraces and direct beach frontage. Realtor’s earlier report on the property described it as a contemporary 4,000-square-foot home with a rare rooftop deck overlooking the Pacific.The house was originally built in the 1990s by the late Jose Liberman of Liberman Broadcasting and remained in the Liberman family for years before Cage acquired it.No immediate confirmation on extent of damage to homeWhile the driveway and surrounding property have suffered substantial damage, it was not immediately clear whether the main structure of Cage’s home had sustained any structural damage.The dramatic incident occurred after a day of heavy rain in the Los Angeles area, with high surf affecting the Southern California coast following the development of Hurricane Marie.Cage, 62, is known for films including Face/Off, Con Air, Gone in 60 Seconds, National Treasure and Moonstruck. He married his fifth wife, Riko Shibata, in 2021.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Brazil Supreme Court rift deepens as justice suspends federal police chief
articles.summary: Allegations of misconduct between two justices threaten to pull court into political battles ahead of upcoming election.
articles.body:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca has ordered the suspension of federal police chief Andrei Rodrigues and the force’s intelligence chief Leandro Almada amid growing divisions that have tested the credibility of the country’s highest court.

The suspensions were announced on Tuesday. Mendonca, appointed by former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, has accused Rodrigues and Almada of producing six illegal reports on the activities of justices.

The move was backed by a majority on one of the high court’s five-member panels.

But it is likely to be challenged by the government, possibly pulling the administration of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva into a political battle ahead of October’s presidential election .

“Investigating possible evidence of crimes is correct,” Institutional Relations Minister Jose Guimaraes, a top aide to Lula, said in response to the decision on social media. “But this measure smells electoral to me. That cannot happen.”

Polls show Lula and Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Senator Flavio Bolsonaro , in a tight race ahead of the first round of voting on October 4.

The Supreme Court has been roiled by mutual accusations of wrongdoing between Justice Alexandre de Moraes , appointed under centre-right President Michel Temer, and Mendonca, a Bolsonaro appointee.

De Moraes has become a prominent target of right-wing criticism, particularly after he oversaw the case against Jair Bolsonaro for plotting a coup after the 2022 election.

A report detailing possible links between de Moraes and disgraced banker Daniel Vorcaro was made public by Mendonca last week.

De Moraes, however, responded by accusing Mendonca of abusing his power, citing federal police intelligence reports and urging the court to investigate him. Mendonca has now challenged the legality of those reports.

The Vorcaro corruption scandal has widened to include powerful political figures on both the left and right.

Vorcaro was arrested in 2025 for allegedly overseeing one of the largest bank fraud schemes in the history of Brazil, leaving billions in owed money.

Flavio Bolsonaro has also faced scrutiny for his ties with Vorcaro, after he approached the banker for assistance in funding a film about his father. Jair Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence.

The right-wing senator used Tuesday’s suspension to push his claim that the prosecution of his father was a political “witch-hunt”. The Federal Police had recommended charges be brought against the elder Bolsonaro in November 2024.

“Lula’s special group in the Federal Police officially unmasked,” Senator Bolsonaro wrote in a social media post. “May the honourable and glorious Federal Police regain its autonomy to go after criminals, and not Lula’s political adversaries.”

William Marcel Murad, the federal police’s executive director, released a statement saying that Rodrigues has the agency’s “full confidence” and that agents “will not be shaken by attacks”.

articles.summary: Experts explain how compression socks may help improve circulation and ease swelling and discomfort, plus the seven pairs they recommend.
articles.body: Whether you spend long days sitting at a desk, are taking a lengthy flight or, conversely, are on your feet for hours at a time, compression socks may help improve circulation and ease swelling, pain and that heavy feeling in your legs. We spoke with experts to find out how compression socks work and which brands are worth trying. Sigvaris, Sockwell and Nurse Yard topped their lists for comfort, style and compression strength. Why do experts recommend compression socks? Inactivity, sitting or standing all day can cause blood pooling, which leads to swelling and an uncomfortable, heavy feeling in the legs, explains Dr. Anne Sharkey, a board-certified podiatrist based in Austin, Texas. Compression socks work "by applying external pressure to the lower legs," which helps move blood back to the heart and reduces blood pooling in the legs, feet and ankles, easing aches and fatigue. "Normally, the muscles in the legs pump and bring back the blood to the heart," Dr. Samantha Landau, professor at Touro New York College of Podiatric Medicine, tells us. With age, genetics, too much pressure on the legs or lack of activity, the valves can weaken. According to Dr. Landau, compression socks help relieve pain and can lower the risk of blood clots. Most experts noted that the level of compression matters over brand popularity. 15–20 mmHg compression socks offer moderate pressure, making them good for daily use. 20–30 mmHg compression socks give stronger, firmer, more restrictive pressure that experts say may be best for pain management. Who should wear compression socks? Compression socks can benefit people who spend long stretches sitting or standing, including passengers on long flights, flight attendants, nurses and office workers, by helping improve circulation and reduce swelling and pain. They’re also commonly worn during pregnancy and postpartum to help with swelling. Athletes often use compression socks during or after workouts to support recovery and relieve muscle strain. The experts also say that patients with chronic leg pain, those who are bedridden and wheelchair users may also benefit from compression socks, depending on their health needs. articles.title: U.S. strikes Iranian tankers after attempted attacks on Navy warship
articles.summary: American forces in the Middle East struck multiple Iranian tankers that U.S. officials said are linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in response to attempted attacks by the IRGC on at least one U.S. ship operating in the region, according to a U.S. official.
articles.body: American forces in the Middle East struck multiple Iranian tankers that U.S. officials said are linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in response to attempted attacks by the IRGC on at least one U.S. ship operating in the region, according to a U.S. official. The Iranian attacks did not hit the ship or injure American personnel, according to the official. The strikes Tuesday on the Iranian tankers come after the IRGC attempted to hit an American aircraft carrier and a destroyer over the weekend, resulting in a U.S. response in which the U.S. sunk one tanker and permanently disabled two more. Iran threatened to target oil tankers in Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for the U.S. strikes. “Following the actions of the American military in targeting several Iranian oil tankers, we warn all oil tanker crews in the areas around the ports of Kuwait and Bahrain, which are hosting these forces and are complicit in their actions, to immediately evacuate their vessels, whether they are at anchor or docked as they will be targeted,” the IRGC Navy said in a statement posted by the semi-official Fars news agency.
